records.quote: Corollary 1. 1. Assume that Y(k) and Z(K) denote the Kth order statistic from samples Y1, Y2, . . . , Ys and Z1, Z2, . . . , Zs, respectively, both of size s. If Y ≤sto Z, then Y(k) ≤sto Z(k), which implies RFGxΦν(Y(k)) ≥ RFGxΦν(Z(k)) for all k = 1, 2, . . . , s, ν ≥ 1.
records.family: general (same marginals Y vs Z), samples of size s
records.compared: kth order statistics of two st-ordered samples

hypotheses.formal: usual stochastic order between the parent variables

conclusion.direction: Y(k) <=st Z(k) (extropy consequence RFGxΦν(Y(k)) >= RFGxΦν(Z(k)) is secondary)

records.ambiguity: Corollary of Theorem 6 (st order is preserved to order statistics); the extropy inequality is a consequence, not a distributional order.

note: Corollary 1 part 1 prints Y(k) <=sto Z(k) under Y <=sto Z — in-scope st conclusion; both passes agree.

records.quote: 2. Assume that Us and Vs correspond to the sth record values from the sequences {Ys, s ≥ 1} and {Zs, s ≥ 1}, respectively. When Y ≤sto Z, it follows that Us ≤sto Vs, and consequently, RFGxΦν(Us) ≥ RFGxΦν(Vs) holds for k = 1, 2, . . . , s, ν ≥ 1.

Theorem 5's conclusion is an inequality between scalar extropy functionals (RFGxΦν), not an ordering of two distributions — the icv order is only the hypothesis. Out of scope per spec.
Theorem 6's conclusion is an extropy inequality RFGxΦν(Y1) <= RFGxΦν(Y2); the st order is only the hypothesis — not a distributional-order conclusion. Out of scope.
Theorem 7(i) bounds RFGxΦν(Y1+Y2) by min of extropies — a functional inequality, not a distributional ordering. Out of scope.
Theorem 7(ii) bounds RFGxΦν(Y1+Y2) by the sum of extropies — a functional inequality, not a distributional ordering. Out of scope.
